name: Multi-Cause Incident Diagnosis and Evidence-Based Replanning
description: Investigate competing production-incident hypotheses, execute one human-authorized remediation, verify partial recovery, and replan toward a remaining downstream cause.
learning_objectives: Distinguish incident symptoms, correlation, supported causal hypotheses, and verified recovery.
Compare rolling-deployment versions with normalized measurements from the same cohort.
Gate privacy-sensitive workload inspection with deterministic database-health evidence.
Keep incident facts, telemetry sources, and approval records outside model-controlled arguments.
Bind human authorization to one incident snapshot, observation, and exact remediation action.
Verify user-facing recovery across sustained post-remediation windows.
Reopen competing hypotheses after partial subsystem recovery instead of declaring success.
Escalate truthfully when an external supported cause keeps the API unhealthy.

messages.content: Investigate incident INC-014. The application owns an immutable incident snapshot and all authoritative evidence. Request at most one tool per response. First call get_incident_details. Then test the deployment hypothesis, inspect database health, and inspect database workloads in that order. Do not claim causation from timing alone and do not invent evidence references. When a supported workload requires remediation, stop calling tools and respond only with JSON containing status needs_approval and a non-empty message that explains the evidence, read/write operation type, resource impact, proposed action, and interruption risk. The application will collect a human decision and provide an immutable authorization. Only then may you call execute_workload_remediation with the exact authorized observation, action, and authorization ID. After execution, call verify_remediation_outcome with the returned remediation execution ID. A recovered database does not prove incident resolution: if the API remains unhealthy, call investigate_downstream_dependency_issue using that same execution ID. If it supports an external dependency as the remaining cause and no further authorized local remediation exists, finish with JSON containing status escalated and a non-empty message. Never expose raw SQL, log text, request payloads, credentials, or customer data.

tools.name: get_incident_details
tools.description: Return API symptoms and a historical healthy baseline from the bound incident snapshot.

tools.name: diagnose_deployment_changes
tools.description: Compare old and new versions in a matched rolling-deployment cohort using trusted evidence.

tools.name: inspect_database_health
tools.description: Return aligned database latency, pressure, data-quality, and timing measurements.

tools.name: inspect_database_workloads
tools.description: After the deterministic health gate passes, return sanitized suspected workload observations without raw SQL or customer data.

tools.name: execute_workload_remediation
tools.description: Execute only the exact workload action allowed by an application-owned human authorization.

tools.name: verify_remediation_outcome
tools.description: Measure sustained database and API recovery after one exact remediation execution.

tools.name: investigate_downstream_dependency_issue
tools.description: Inspect registered downstream dependencies after verified partial recovery and return sanitized causal evidence.
